title: The Lion Cave Is Betrayed to the Mughals

blocks.text: Inside the cave, the hidden Singhs preserve a strict communal ethic, sharing whatever food can be gathered and making room for any brother who reaches the refuge. Small night journeys for grain and vegetables keep them alive, but the arrangement remains precarious because concealment is their only shield.

That shield fails when the cave is betrayed to the Mughals, who learn who is inside and close in around the refuge. Laddha Singh Bhangoo, Ram Singh, and Sulakhan Singh Gill are identified, and the attackers begin to treat the cave like a trap that can be reduced by patience and force.

The besiegers choose musket smoke as their first main method, hoping to suffocate or drive the Singhs out without facing their resistance in open combat. The page thus turns the cave from sanctuary into a battlefield shaped by confinement, ingenuity, and endurance.
